conclusion: No actionable material blocker for the current opt-in projection and documented audit contract. Preserve defaultfull and same projection in both memory arms. Any future benchmark must charge complete trace/I/O/storage and cannot infer benefit from response bytes alone.

confirmed.finding: Only the named provenance/hash fields are removed. Complete note strings, exact entry IDs, note keys, subject selectors, typed expectations, labels, availability, state_type, freshness, errors and withheld reason/actions are retained in the closed backend schema.

Projection is applied once after either backend lookup, with no backend/arm branch. Ranking, original16KiBselection budget, selected records, unavailable withholding and error handling are unchanged. No historical fallback or replacement candidates are introduced.

Receipt binds canonical full MCP result, compact result before receipt and final model-facing result via full SHA256 digests, including isError. Independent hashlib/json verification passed and rejects single full/model/receipt tampering.

Audit trace append occurs before compact result return. Its OSError propagates through serve before that tool JSON-RPC response is written; independent stdio control emitted only initialization reply.

Default full results and full trace shape matched the installed adapter under the same authored backend and deterministic clocks. CLI defaults full. Additional compact_response.py must be installed with the adapter as README states.

Projection, parsing/canonicalization and digest work occur inside lookup timing. Full audit trace serialization/append and JSON-RPC output are excluded from this local timer and require outer lifecycle/I/O/storage accounting. response_bytes is complete MCP result bytes, not tokens.

limitations_not_blockers.detail: Unkeyed hashes are evidence bindings, not signatures, append-only storage or current-fact validation. Verification requires authentic retained full audit data and pinned projector/trace identity; a party replacing both trace and model result can recompute hashes.

Credential/email redaction can change bound bytes and must make original receipt verification fail against the scrubbed copy. README explicitly states pre-publication verification and forbids silent rebinding/redaction bypass.

Successful append is not fsync/power-loss durability. Partial/failed append terminates without releasing that response; previous evidence preservation/publication remains the outer harness responsibility.
Projector assumes current internal one-text-block MCP result and dictionary-shaped payload. It is not a generic arbitrary MCP result transformer. Current adapter constructs exactly that schema.

Model loses direct source hashes/catalog/snapshot/generation IDs and instead receives one audit receipt. Exact source selectors/trust/freshness remain, and full provenance is audit-side. This is an explicit opt-in display tradeoff.

Receipt/error overhead can enlarge empty/error responses; complete audit objects increase stored bytes and serialization work. Reported preserved-response byte savings do not establish token/billing/quality/wall improvements. This review did not read/re-measure actual task model responses.

review_kind: independent read-only source review plus authored fixture controls

No CAMI registration/refresh or actual backend lifecycle performance experiment
